plan.purpose: ThunderKittens vs TileLang R splitting on H100: same algorithm in both (cluster of k CTAs, WGMMA with the R slice as operand A, h slices exchanged by bulk shared::cluster copies completing on the receiver's mbarrier, no per-step cluster barrier); each also against Triton R tiling (L2 barrier); kernel-level comparison at T=1024 isolates the R-splitting kernels from each framework's launch path, the classifier rows include it
plan.workload: external-baseline classifier as in M4: 4 layers, vocab 512, FP16, (B,C,T) in (1,8,32),(16,32,32),(32,64,128); D in 192,256,384,512
plan.protocol: phase 0 cell checks (hidden + FP32 carry vs FP64 GPU oracle, CELL_BUDGET, FP16, LSTM warm / sLSTM zero,mixed,warm, (3,17,2),(16,128,1)); split-0 selection among passing configurations -> frozen hashed table -> split-1 timing 5 starts x 20 ABBA/BAAB blocks; model-budget checks of every arm vs FP64 model oracle and arm-vs-arm before timing; hierarchical bootstrap seed 20261013+index
plan.node_reason: One ACC node (4 H100): four single-GPU lanes pinned to GPU-local cores; checks and selection behind barriers before timing
deviations: ThunderKittens and TileLang paths implement the spike contract (one full logical call, hidden history and FP32 final carry), not chunk continuation or full-state output
TileLang v2 issues two block barriers before the exchange copies (one explicit, one inserted by TileLang); ThunderKittens issues one
barrier arming differs by framework idiom: ThunderKittens receiver arms expect_tx once per step; TileLang copy_cluster sender does one remote arrive.expect_tx per copy
not_claimed: TileLang or ThunderKittens ceiling beyond this algorithm
plan.kernel_level: primary R-splitting comparison: preallocated FP16 inputs, H=1, T=1024, B in 16,64, D in 192,256,384,512; CUDA-event time per call; 5 starts x 20 ABBA/BAAB blocks; CELL_BUDGET vs FP64 and arm-vs-arm; repeated outputs must stay bit-identical

predecessor.result: TileLang v2 first cell check BACKEND_ERROR (barrier hang trapped as launch failure); ThunderKittens 20/20 available; 40 TK-vs-Triton comparisons completed
predecessor.diagnosis: debug jobs 47301592/47301920: synchronous-exchange variant correct; bulk variant hung in Barrier::wait because TileLang tma_store_cluster arms the remote barrier itself (arrive.expect_tx per copy) while the receiver also armed it with count 1
predecessor.repair: receiver barrier count k-1, no receiver-side expect_tx (TileLang copy_cluster convention)
